what_happened.line: The Economic Development Committee spent most of the meeting planning a September meet-and-greet for local business owners and town officials.
Six tables are needed and Parks and Rec is to be asked for them; a church is to be asked about chairs.
The committee has no budget for event supplies, so members agreed to make personal donations toward costs.
Town employees cannot solicit donations but can publicize that donation opportunities exist; if alcohol is served, it will be beer and wine only.
No formal votes were audible; the next meeting was set for Thursday, September 14, at six o'clock.

why_it_matters: Events meant to draw local businesses to town have no line in the town budget, so they depend on volunteer donations and ethics-limited sponsorship rather than appropriated money.
The committee also heard updates on a solar parking-lot bylaw intended for fall town meeting and on the Master Plan, both of which could reach residents as later votes.

meetings.headline: Economic Development Committee kept planning its business event despite the Business Association declining to take part.
meetings.summary: The committee reviewed a draft town-official meet-and-greet flyer, then spent most of the meeting on the Lunenburg Business Association's unexplained decision not to be involved in the planned event and whether to go ahead without it. Members also heard new-business and master plan updates. The only motion captured was to close the meeting.

budget_items.what_was_said: A member said funding food is the challenge and offered to pay personally. Others suggested low-cost options such as trays, store-bought platters or sponsorship.
A member reported the association's dumpster-day and charity golf fundraisers to support its events.

decisions.decision: A staff member will contact the Business Association's president and share the outcome with members by email, as informational only, ideally before the association's next meeting.
The event date, time and concept will be raised at next Tuesday's department head meeting.
One member will meet with the town's social media coordinator about the flyer, and the committee will drive the content. No objection was voiced.
The committee leaned toward proceeding with the event and inviting the Business Association, unless it raises significant concerns.
